title: Revealing Floating-Point Accumulation Orders in Software/Hardware Implementations
problem: Accumulation orders in software and hardware implementations are undocumented, making it difficult for developers to ensure consistent results across systems and verify implementation equivalence.
motivation: Understanding and verifying consistent accumulation orders is essential for reproducible scientific computing and ensuring correctness of deep learning implementations across different platforms.
method: FPRev reveals the accumulation order (the order in which a system adds floating-point numbers—decimal numbers represented in computers) without modifying code or hardware. It tests the system with carefully chosen numerical inputs and observes the output differences, since different addition orders produce different results. By analyzing these output patterns, FPRev determines which order was used, and the efficient test design makes this faster than checking all possible sequences.
key_novelty: It reveals the accumulation order (the sequence of additions) by analyzing how outputs vary with carefully chosen numerical tests, rather than requiring inspection of the implementation code or hardware.
contributions: FPRev: diagnostic tool to reveal accumulation orders in software/hardware implementations non-intrusively
Comprehensive characterization of accumulation orders in NumPy and PyTorch across CPU and GPU platforms including specialized accelerators
Efficient diagnostic algorithm with lower time complexity than basic solutions
Open-source tool enabling reproducible computational verification

metrics.other: lower time complexity of diagnostic tool vs basic solution; characterization of accumulation orders

limitations: Paper focuses on diagnostic approach rather than implementation optimization; limitations regarding scalability or applicability not discussed.
